title: Floods.
paragraphs:
Floods.
Fasting.
Wilderness.
Waiting.
If you read the Bible carefully, you will begin to notice something fascinating.
One number appears again… and again… and again.

It shows up in storms.
It shows up in deserts.
It shows up in seasons of prayer, testing, and preparation.
And the question many readers quietly ask is this:
Why does the Bible keep repeating the number 40?
Is it coincidence?
Or is God revealing a pattern?
The first time many people notice this number is in the story of Noah.
When God judged the earth because of human corruption, rain fell for 40 days and 40 nights.

Not 12.
Not 7.
Not 100.
Forty.
During those forty days, the old world was washed away.
But those same forty days also prepared the earth for a new beginning.
Judgment… followed by renewal.
Already the pattern begins.
Later in Scripture, we see the same number again.
When God called Moses to receive the Law, Moses went up Mount Sinai and stayed in the presence of God for 40 days and 40 nights (Exodus 34:28).

No food.
No water.
Just the overwhelming presence of God.
And when Moses came down the mountain, he carried the commandments that would shape the entire life of the Israelites.
Think about that.
Before the Law was given…
Before a nation was shaped…
There was 40 days in the presence of God.
Preparation always comes before impact.
Then the pattern expands even further.
Because the people of Israel themselves entered a season defined by the same number.
After leaving Egypt, they wandered in the wilderness for 40 years before entering the Promised Land (Numbers 14:33–34).
Forty years of learning.
Forty years of testing.
Forty years of God shaping a former slave population into a people who would learn to trust Him.
The wilderness was not wasted time.
It was formation time.
Centuries later, another prophet appears in the story.
After a moment of deep discouragement, Elijah traveled 40 days and 40 nights through the wilderness to Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:8).
This journey came after one of the greatest victories in his life.
Yet even after victory, Elijah needed a season where God would restore his perspective.
Sometimes the wilderness is not punishment.
Sometimes it is restoration.
And then the pattern reaches its most powerful moment.
Before beginning His public ministry, Jesus Christ went into the wilderness and fasted for 40 days (Matthew 4:2).
Forty days of hunger.
Forty days of temptation.
Forty days of solitude.
Only after that wilderness season did Jesus step forward and begin preaching, healing, and revealing the Kingdom of God.
Even the Son of God entered a season of testing before public ministry began.
When you step back and look at all of these moments together, something remarkable becomes clear.
In Scripture, 40 often marks a season of testing, preparation, purification, or transition before something new begins.
It is the space between chapters.
The bridge between calling and fulfillment.
The wilderness between promise and arrival.
This matters more than many people realize.
Because when we go through seasons that feel slow, silent, or difficult…
We often assume nothing important is happening.
But the Bible shows a different pattern.
God frequently does His deepest work during hidden seasons.
No crowds.
No applause.
No recognition.
Just formation.
The flood prepared a new world.
Sinai prepared a nation.
The wilderness prepared Israel.
The desert prepared Jesus.
And in many lives today, God still uses wilderness seasons to prepare people for what comes next.
Not everything meaningful happens in moments of visibility.
Sometimes destiny is formed in the quiet places.
Here is a powerful truth many people overlook:

The wilderness is not where God abandons people.
It is often where He prepares them.
Testing strengthens faith.
Waiting builds endurance.
Solitude deepens dependence on God.
And what feels like delay may actually be divine preparation.
So if you find yourself in a season that feels like waiting…
A season that feels like stretching…
A season that feels quiet and uncertain…
You might be standing in your own version of a “forty season.”
A place where God is shaping something deeper than what people can see.
Because throughout Scripture, one pattern remains consistent:

Testing first.
Preparation second.
Purpose next.
And sometimes…
The most important chapters of your life are being written in the seasons that look the quietest.
“God often prepares people in the wilderness before revealing their purpose in the world.”
“The season that feels slow may actually be the season where God is building strength.”
“What looks like delay may actually be preparation.”
Now a question for you:
Have you ever experienced a “wilderness season” that later prepared you for something greater?
Share your story below. Your testimony might encourage someone who is walking through their own season of 40.
